title: fix(plugin-approvals): an approval request is titled by its flow's label, never the raw record id or the flow's machine name
body:
Fixes #24665

Clause-②: no

objectstack-ai/objectui#12484 remains blocked until the console pin bump.

## What changes

The served approval request page (`sys_approval_request_detail`) authors no header, so the console titles it from the object's declaration over the row the approvals get serves: the `nameField` value, then the deprecated `titleFormat` only where that value is empty (ADR-0079). The pointer was `display_title`, a formula. A formula has no stored column and `rowFromRequest` serves none, so every page fell through to `{process_name} · {record_id}`: `flow:NAME · RECORD_ID` as its H1.

`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts`:

- `nameField` and `displayNameField` become `process_label`, the stored flow-label column. The approvals get already serves it (`rowFromRequest`, through the display-label chain: the column, else the config snapshot's `__flowLabel`, else the humanized machine name). So the page's H1 is the flow's label in every subject state, and the get serves the declared `nameField` value. No change to `approval-service.ts` and no new key on `ApprovalRequestRow`: the route needs no spec change.
- `titleFormat` becomes `{process_name}`, without `{record_id}`. A renderer reaches it only where `process_label` is empty (a row written before the column, until the boot backfill labels it). The approvals get never reaches it.
- `display_title` stays declared. Its expression drops the ` · record_id` half: `process_label`, else `process_name`. That is the text the title ladder draws on the data door for every row the engine writes. Its help text and the three translated locales say so. `en` was regenerated with the package's documented `os i18n extract` command (via `packages/cli/bin/run-dev.js`), and `--check` reports 7 bundles in sync.

The subject record stays named by the Details tab's reference card (`record_id` / `object_name`). That card handles the readable, deleted and unresolvable states, which a title cannot.

## Acceptance

1. **The approvals get serves the declared `nameField` value, and a pin holds it.** New `sys-approval-request-title.integration.test.ts` uses the real `ApprovalService` on real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver`. The declaration's `nameField` is `process_label`, a `text` field with a real DDL column, and `getRequest` and `listRequests` serve the same non-empty value under it.
2. **The H1 names no raw record id and no `flow:` machine name, in each state, one pin per state.** Readable (`Rd4bl3Rec24665QQ`, opened by the service), deleted (subject deleted, request `cancelled` / `record_deleted`) and unresolvable (`object_name` names an object the registry does not hold). In each, the served title equals the flow label, is non-blank, does not contain the record id and does not match `flow:`. A fourth case: a row with no stored label and no snapshot label is served the humanized machine name (`Invoice Approval`), so the template is never reached on this door.
3. **The search palette follows the same title.** `#24087` (PR #24202) made `searchAll`'s `renderTitle` read the `nameField` value first (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, `titlePointer` then `titleFormatSource`), pinned by `protocol.search-title-namefield.test.ts` ("THE PIN — an object declaring both keys is titled by its nameField value"). The palette's `engine.find` row carries the stored `process_label`, so a request is listed under its flow label. On an unlabelled pre-backfill row it draws `{process_name}`, the same fallback as the data door. No new palette pin: `packages/metadata-protocol` is outside this claim's file surface, and the order is already pinned there.

`sys-approval-display-title.test.ts` flips. The request now resolves to `process_label`. A labelled row's H1, `display_title` and `resolveRecordTitle` are all `Discount Sign-off`, with no `· opp_45`. An unlabelled row's pointer value is empty, and the template and `display_title` both draw `flow:deal_desk` (never `null`, never the id). `resolveRecordTitle` answers `undefined` there: the accessor reads the pointer and never invents a title.

## The open choice inside A1, read on the four axes

**`display_title`: retire or keep?** The dispatch said to retire it if nothing but the title ladder reads it. Something else does read it. The activity mirror (`plugin-audit` `audit-writers.ts`) stores the title field's name as the provenance of each activity row's `summary` and `record_label` (`text_sources`, from `titleFieldOf`). The read side (`activity-field-redaction.ts` `sourcesServed`) serves those texts only while every named field is in the reader's served set. So retiring the field would withhold the summary and label of every `sys_approval_request` activity row written while it was the title. The 18.0 upgrade fixture's `database.sql` carries that `text_sources` shape on other objects' `display_title`. This is a code reading. Activity redaction was not run for this object.

- Real business need: the stored provenance is a measured reader. A zero-consumer field would be retired; this one is not zero-consumer.
- Long-term soundness: one stored column is the title on every door. The formula is kept only as a computed mirror of that same text, with no second source.
- Keeping AI from writing it wrong: the kept formula now equals the title, so a field labelled "Title" no longer serves a different text (with a raw id) than the record's heading.
- No scope creep at startup: retiring it would be a narrowing (BREAKING `minor`, an ADR-0087 marker, a contract review) whose cost falls on stored history. Keeping it adds nothing and declares nothing new.

Recommendation taken: keep it, with the reason in the field's comment. This PR therefore narrows nothing and carries `Clause-②: no` with a `patch` changeset (`.changeset/24665-approval-request-title.md`). That follows the newest plugin-approvals convention on `main` (`.changeset/24375-approval-object-chip.md`, `24501-list-object-column.md`: a `patch` for a shipped object's display change, with no key added or removed).

**`titleFormat`: drop or keep as `{process_name}`?** Kept, at `{process_name}`. Dropping it would make the unlabelled-row fallback differ by consumer. objectui's derivation would land on a `_title` / `_name` affix field, which is the machine name again. `searchAll`'s candidate list holds none of this object's fields, so it would fall to `String(row.id)`, the request's own id. Keeping it gives every door the same machine-name fallback, which `display_title` also draws. The key is deprecated and lint-advisory platform-wide: 66 `*.object.ts` files in `packages/` declare it. Retiring it is not this card's subject.

## Verification

All on head `1b47ec0748`, worktree off `origin/main`, merged with `origin/main` at `9e2722a92`.

- Closure build: `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@objectstack/plugin-approvals^...' build`, which reported `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals test`: `Test Files 85 passed (85)`, `Tests 1146 passed (1146)`, which reported `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals typecheck`: `check:test-typecheck: OK`, which reported `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The first run caught 3 TS2345 errors in the new test's helper typing, fixed in `test(plugin-approvals): type the served-title helper over the row contract`.
- Ablations: one per changed behaviour, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit 1 to 0, blob changed) with a trap restore. Each restore was proven: the blob equals the HEAD blob and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The subject is imported relatively from `src/`, so no `dist` leg applies.
  - A, pointer back to `display_title`: 7 failed of 11. The served title is `undefined` (`expected 'undefined' to be 'string'`), which is the defect's own mechanism.
  - B, formula back to `· record_id`: 2 failed of 11.
  - C, template back to `{process_name} · {record_id}`: 3 failed of 11.
- Gates: 67 families, derived by `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `1b47ec0748`. They ran locally, with each exit code captured before any pipe: 65 exited 0 and 2 exited 3.
  - The two exit-3 families are NOT MEASURED locally (PREREQUISITE NOT MET). `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` needs every package's `dist/`. `pnpm check:i18n` needs the built CLI; the package's documented extract command, run through `run-dev.js` with `--check`, reports 7 bundles in sync. CI runs both.
  - `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` first exited 3, because its pinned positive control was unreachable on the shallow clone. After fetching that commit it exited 0.
  - `--ran` reconciliation: 67 derived, 65 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED (derived from the recorded exit 3), 0 UNRUN.
  - Not run locally: the vitest `repo` project (`test:repo`). This diff touches none of its tests, and CI's `Test Core` runs it.

## Acceptance notes

- objectui's console fixtures (`apps/console/src/services/approvalRequestsDataSource.servedPage*.test.tsx`) copy the request definition with `nameField: 'display_title'`. They are copies, not readers, and they change with the console pin bump that objectstack-ai/objectui#12484 waits on. Carrier: that card's dev.
- `sys_approval_approver`'s title is `{approver} · {request_id}` (`role:finance · areq_…`), which also prints a raw id. Observation only: the reach was not measured, and that index object is not on the request page. Carrier: none.
- `resolveRecordTitle(SysApprovalRequest, row)` on a row with no stored label now answers `undefined`, where it answered `flow:NAME · RECORD_ID` before. Server-side consumers (the activity `record_label`, lookup titles) see no title for such a row until the boot backfill labels it, which it does for every request.
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.search-title-namefield.test.ts:185` describes `sys_approval_request`'s old declaration as the defect it pinned. That is historical and accurate, with its own inline fixture. Left as is (outside the file surface).
